title: Three-dimensional deep learning nomogram for post-plan quality assurance in high-dose-rate prostate brachytherapy☆
creator: Joel Beaudry, Tonghe Wang, Shirin A. Enger, Antonio L. Damato
description: PurposeClassical nomograms for high-dose-rate (HDR) prostate brachytherapy quality assurance (QA) evaluate agreement between planned and expected total dwell time but do not directly assess the three-dimensional treated volume. This study's aim was to develop a deep learning-based 3D nomogram to predict institution-specific clinical 100% isodose volumes from anatomy and dwell positions for post-plan QA.

title: Metabolomics workbench: data-driven classification and correlation analysis between metabolite classes, biomarkers, and drugs
creator: Mikhail M Khandokhin, Aleksandr Sokolov, Nikolay Oskolkov, Robert Fredriksson, Olga E Titova, Helgi B Schiöth
description: Public repositories now accumulate an unprecedented amount of metabolomics data. Despite the opportunities for large-scale meta-analyses opened by these repositories, the deposited data rarely becomes systematically re-analyzed. We conducted a systematic metadata-based re-analysis of all human blood metabolomics studies in the Metabolomics Workbench performed using Orbitrap or QTOF mass spectrometry, encompassing 44 165 samples.

title: Response to Khodamoradi: Methodological clarifications regarding NanOx predictions in helium SOBP
creator: Thomas Berger, Gersende Alphonse, Mario Alcocer-Avila, Caterina Monini, Charbel Koumeir, Claire Rodriguez-Lafrasse, Nicolas Varmenot, Vincent Métivier, Ferid Haddad, Jean Michel Létang, Étienne Testa

title: Combined Day–Night Heat Damage in Soybean Is Driven by Nighttime Warming
creator: Gabriel Ferraz Guimarães, Jéssica de Jesus Santos, Rafael Vasconcelos Ribeiro, Milton Costa Lima Neto
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Asymmetric warming, characterized by faster increases in nighttime than daytime temperatures, is an emerging threat to crop performance. However, the interactive physiological effects of day versus night heat remain insufficiently resolved in soybean ( Glycine max L. Here, we evaluated soybean responses to 4 day/night thermal regimes (28°C/22°C, 40°C/22°C, 28°C/28°C, and 40°C/28°C) to test whether nighttime warming is the dominant driver of stress disruption. Isolated daytime heat (40°C/22°C) enhanced photosynthetic performance and maintained biomass, indicating short‐term functional plasticity.

title: ‘It Makes Me Feel Confident’: A Community Based Participatory Study of Experiences of Employment for People With Intellectual Disabilities
creator: Deanna Gallichan, Chloe Deacon, Karen Gresty, Simon Rundle
description: BackgroundA social enterprise brewery requested help from researchers to understand their employment opportunities for people with intellectual disabilities (‘trainees’). A community‐based participatory framework (CBPR) was used to develop the research.MethodDigital storytelling was selected to enable trainees to express their views about their work. Six participants created digital stories with support from researchers.

title: Biosolids in Washington State: Putting per‐ and poly‐fluorinated alkyl substances concerns into a real‐world context
creator: Sally Brown, Scott Mansell
description: Washington State has a history of beneficial use of municipal biosolids. The Department of Ecology recently conducted a voluntary survey of per‐ and poly‐fluorinated alkyl substances (PFAS) in biosolids. Results of that survey are presented and compared with the results from mandatory sampling in Michigan.

title: The forgotten organ: Why the oral microbiome belongs in every physician's toolkit
creator: Victoria Sampson
description: The oral cavity is the most densely colonised microbial niche in the human body after the gut – over 700 species and an estimated two billion bacteria (Deo and Deshmukh, 2019) – yet it remains conspicuously absent from the systemic health conversation.

title: The hidden consequences of marine heatwaves: rising Vibrio risk in European coastal waters
creator: Jan C Semenza, Joaquin A Trinanes, Jaime Martinez-Urtaza
description: heatwaves dominate public attention, because of their immediate impacts on human health, they often overshadow equally profound changes occurring in the oceans. During the same month, the western Mediterranean Sea and adjacent Atlantic coastal waters experienced a record-breaking marine heatwave.

title: Decoupling Transparency and Electron Injection in Ultrathin Ag Electrodes Using an Al/MoO3 Double Seed Layer for Transparent Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Diodes
creator: Yeyun Bae, Kyoungeun Lee, Kyunghoon Lee, Jaeyeop Lee, Jiyoon Oh, Jiwoong Yang, Chansu Kim, Jeongkyun Roh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). There is growing interest in transparent quantum dot light‐emitting diodes (Tr‐QLEDs) for window‐type displays. For such devices, the top transparent electrode must simultaneously provide high optical transmittance, low sheet resistance, and efficient charge injection. Ultrathin Ag films are promising because of their high conductivity and transparency, but they tend to grow via the Volmer–Weber mode, resulting in poor continuity and increased resistance.

title: Surrogate Scattering Matrix‐Guided Inverse Design of Nanophotonic Neural Networks
creator: Azka Maula Iskandar Muda, Uğur Teğin
description: Optical computing offers a route to address the growing computational demands of machine learning, with inverse‐designed nanophotonic media providing a compact path to passive optical operators. Training such devices end to end remains expensive because each geometry update requires full‐wave forward and adjoint evaluations. We introduce a surrogate‐guided inverse‐design framework that separates task learning from electromagnetic realization.

title: The FHJ debate: Dental health is so crucial that it should be in the medical school curriculum
creator: Jasmine Ho, Clarissa Hjalmarsson
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This debate article evaluates whether dental health education should be more widely integrated into the undergraduate medical curriculum. The authors present evidence-informed arguments situated within an evolving landscape of healthcare delivery, professional expectations, and political system-level pressures. Central to both perspectives is the need to advocate for patients’ best interests, along with the practicalities of implementing an integrated, cross-disciplinary healthcare curriculum.

title: Antioxidant therapy, N-acetyl-L-cysteine, effects on pancreatic β cells: therapeutic promise or potential harm?
creator: Meg Schuurman, Jonathan Nguyen, Malina Barillaro, Nica Borradaile, Rennian Wang
description: N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) is a widely used antioxidant with increasing public interest in its use for treating metabolic disease, yet its effects on pancreatic β cells remain incompletely understood. Most studies focus on NAC's benefits under pathological conditions—such as obesity, high-fat diet exposure, and type 2 diabetes—where oxidative stress impairs β-cell function, identity, and survival.

title: Neurofilaments support the differentiation of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis from degenerative cervical myelopathy
creator: Julia Goebell, Franziska Bachhuber, Jutta Karmann, Veronika Klose, Jan Kassubek, Hans-Peter Müller, Hayrettin Tumani, Albert Ludolph
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The differential diagnosis between degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM) and early amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is often clinically challenging; laboratory tests that support this distinction could be highly valuable. This study examined the concentrations of neurofilament light chain (NfL) and the phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNfH), in CSF and serum of carefully selected patients with DCM, spinal canal stenosis (SCS) and ALS, after exclusion of major neurological confounders. Patients were assigned to five groups according to MRI findings and ALS diagnosis.

title: Risk of atrial fibrillation according to electrocardiographic risk factors: a nationwide cohort study of 1.5 million patients
creator: Casper Binding, Christoffer Polcwiartek, Kristian Kragholm, Sam Riahi, Mikkel Porsborg Andersen, Helle Collatz Christensen, Mohamad Hassan El-Chouli, Signe Juul Riddersholm, Lise Da Riis-Vestergaard, Peter Søgaard, Gregory Y H Lip, Christian Torp-Pedersen, Daniel Friedman, Anders Nissen Bonde, Claus
description: AimsAtrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with an increased risk of stroke, yet no evidence exists on the collective effect of electrocardiogram (ECG) risk factors in early detection of AF. We aimed to evaluate the risk of new-onset AF and stroke according to specific ECG risk factors to identify patients at high risk of developing AF.

title: Targeting calciphylaxis: the emergence of vitamin K as a potential treatment
creator: Maria Fusaro, Smeeta Sinha, Antonio Bellasi, Markus Ketteler, Carlo Alfieri, Martin H de Borst, Ditte Hansen, Pietro Manuel Ferraro, Juan Miguel Díaz-Tocados, Mathias Haarhaus, Mehmet Kanbay, Maurizio Gallieni, Paolo Simioni, Sandro Giannini, Sharon Huish, Althea Cossettini
description: Calciphylaxis, or calcific uraemic arteriolopathy, is a rare, life-threatening vascular disorder predominantly affecting patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), especially those on dialysis. It is characterized by arteriolar calcification, thrombosis, and painful ischemic skin lesions that frequently ulcerate, contributing to high morbidity and mortality. Calciphylaxis arises from medial arterial calcification, endothelial injury, and a pro-inflammatory, pro-thrombotic milieu.

title: Interventional radiation immune-boosting (iRIB). The role of concomitant interventional radiotherapy (modern brachytherapy) in immunotherapy: A hypothesis-generating systematic review
creator: Roberta Muni, Valentina Lancellotta, Bruno Fionda, Enrico Rosa, Piotr Wojcieszek, Roberto Iacovelli, Monica Mangoni, Gabriella Macchia, Alessio Giuseppe Morganti, Maria Antonietta Gambacorta, Roberto Iezzi, Luca Tagliaferri
description: PurposeSynergistic activity of radiation and immunotherapy is well known to the extent that it can be referred to as radiation immuno-boosting. Interventional radiotherapy (IRT; modern brachytherapy) has a potential immunomodulatory advantage compared with external beam radiotherapy due to highly conformal dose distribution and dose heterogeneity, engaging multiple immunogenic mechanisms with distinct dose-response profiles.

title: From detection to action: Transparency, accuracy, and integration for clinical artificial intelligence in musculoskeletal aging
creator: Ta-Wei Tai, Dung Van Tran
description: trates how AI can extract additional clinical information from images obtained during routine care, enabling earlier identification of individuals who might otherwise remain unscreened. AI may accelerate screening, automate selected screening tasks, extend clinical capacity, and support case finding in regions where dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and trained personnel are limited.

title: KAT-Net: a hyperbolic routing framework for joint lysine acylation site prediction with shared sequence–structure representations
creator: Hao Wu, Yiyu Lin, Lun Zhu, Yan Wang, Shan Chang, Sen Yang
description: Protein lysine acylation regulates protein function through changes in local chemistry, structure, and molecular interactions. Acetylation (Kac), succinylation (Ksucc), and crotonylation (Kcr) share the lysine centre but differ in acyl-group chemistry, motivating joint yet task-aware prediction. We developed KAT-Net, a multi-task framework integrating ESM-2 representations, physicochemical priors, and AlphaFold2-derived structural context.

title: Epidemiology, risk factors and clinical outcome of community-acquired pneumonia in severely immunosuppressed patients: a comprehensive analysis from the multinational, prospective CAPNETZ Cohort
creator: Stephanie Müller, Gopinath Krishnamoorthy, Grit Barten-Neiner, Gernot Rohde, Mathias W. Pletz, Jessica Rademacher, Jan Rupp, Martin Witzenrath, Andreas Essig, Paul Schmidt, Marcus Panning, Benjamin Thomas Schleenvoigt, Martin Kolditz, M. Dreher, M. Dreher, C. Cornelissen, W. Knüppel, D. Stolz, N. Su
description: PurposeDespite growing evidence that immunosuppression (IS) influences aetiology and prognosis of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), there remains a lack of data from representative multicentre studies.MethodsThe multinational prospective CAPNETZ study includes patients with CAP and HIV since 2017, and with other causes of IS since 2020.

title: Characterizing the credentialed bachelor's-level behavioral health support workforce: a national descriptive study
creator: Brianna M Lombardi, Lisa D Zerden, Maria Gaiser
description: IntroductionPersistent shortages of the behavioral health workforce have prompted interest in expanding roles for bachelor's-level behavioral health support workers as a strategy for increasing care. States vary in how they regulate this workforce. This study characterized how US states define the bachelor's-level behavioral health workforce through credentialing structures, educational requirements, and scope of practice.

title: A collaborative hybrid network with aggregated attention for pulmonary nodule detection
creator: Jianle Chen, Jianyu Zhu, Yiying Wang, Yuyan Lin, Huilian Liao
description: BackgroundLung cancer remains one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, underscoring the critical importance of early detection for improving patient survival. Current imaging‑based methods for pulmonary nodule (PN) detection are often limited by low efficiency and suboptimal accuracy, falling short of the demands for precise clinical diagnosis.

title: Effects of morning versus evening high-intensity exercise on electroencephalographic and autonomic responses in middle-aged women
creator: Jae-Myun Ko, Wi-Young So, Jae-Hyun Jung
description: [Purpose] The time of day at which exercise is performed influences physiological responses and performance, and thus its health benefits. This study investigated whether electroencephalographic (EEG) and autonomic nervous system responses to morning versus evening exercise differed in middle-aged women.[Methods] Thirty women aged 50-60 years were randomly assigned to a morning or evening exercise group.

title: Human–artificial intelligence collaboration in emergency medical services: from diagnostic algorithms to shared decision support
creator: Hang A Park
description: ance comparable to, and in some cases better than, conventional methods [3]. AI-assisted ECG interpretation has reduced inappropriate catheterization laboratory activations, and retrieval-augmented large language models have shown potential for improving the consistency of prehospital triage [4–6]. Natural language processing has also been used in emergency dispatch calls to support earlier recognition of time-critical conditions, including out-of-hospital cardiac arrest [2].

title: A complementary amino acid formulation enhances exercise-induced skeletal muscle remodeling during resistance training
creator: Deunsol Hwang, Sunghwan Kyun, Inkwon Jang, Taeho Kim, Nayeon Kim, Jungyong Lee, Hun-Young Park, Sung-Woo Kim, Insu Kwon, Ahjin Kim, Hangsu Cho, Taehyeon Park, Soohan Jung, Jisu Kim, Kiwon Lim
description: [Purpose] This study investigated whether a five-amino-acid formulation integrating complementary anabolic, metabolic, and redox-supporting functions enhances skeletal muscle remodeling during resistance training.[Methods] Male C57BL/6N mice were assigned to eight groups receiving vehicle, leucine (300 mg/kg), or amino acid formulation (150-1,500 mg/kg). All mice completed four weeks of ladder resistance training, while the assigned supplements were administered orally once daily.

title: Effects of keiser-assisted Nordic hamstring curl training on hamstring flexibility, mechanical properties, and pitching performance in high school baseball pitchers
creator: Ye-Jun Han, Hyun Ahn, Sea-Hyun Bae, Kyung-Yoon Kim
description: [Purpose] This study aimed to investigate the effects of 10-week Keiser-assisted Nordic hamstring curl (NHC) training on the mechanical properties, muscle strength, and flexibility of the hamstrings, as well as shoulder range of motion (ROM) and pitching performance in high school baseball pitchers.[Methods] Sixteen high school baseball pitchers performed Keiser assisted NHC training for 10 weeks.

title: Effects of a low-protein, high-fructose corn syrup diet on skeletal muscle and bone in young adult mice: a pilot study
creator: Hyerim Park
description: [Purpose] This study aimed to examine the effects of chronic consumption of a low-protein diet combined with 10% high-fructose corn syrup (HFCS) on skeletal muscle and bone health in mice. [Methods] Seven-week-old male C57BL/6 mice were fed either a normal diet or a low-protein diet supplemented with 10% HFCS for 12 weeks.

title: Analysis of Postoperative Quality of Life in Patients With Acute Type A Aortic Dissection After Extensive Arch Repair via Partial Upper Sternotomy
creator: Linfeng Xie, Xiujuan Wang, Zhaofeng Zhang, Debin Jiang, Xinfan Lin
description: Background:This study aimed to compare health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with acute type A aortic dissection (AAAD) who underwent extensive arch repair via partial upper sternotomy (PUS) or full median sternotomy (FS).Methods:Data were collected from 112 patients with AAAD who were divided into two groups based on the surgical approach.

title: Early Initiation of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure: Efficacy, Safety, and Implementation in Stabilized Patients
creator: Alfredo Mauriello, Adriana Correra, Anna Chiara Maratea, Valeria Cetoretta, Francesco Giallauria, Giovanni Esposito, Alfonso Desiderio, Francesco Sabatella, Renato Gioia, Gemma Marrazzo, Biagio Liccardo, Vincenzo Russo, Paolo Trambaiolo, Antonello D’Andrea
description: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have fundamentally reshaped the pharmacological management of chronic heart failure (HF). However, the role of these inhibitors during the vulnerable phase of acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) has historically been limited by concerns regarding hemodynamic stability and renal function.

title: Population-based registry analysis of cervical cancer trends in Tashkent, Uzbekistan 2014-2024
creator: Ulugbek Khudayberdievich Mirzaev, Jasur Ravshanovich Juraev, Iroda Pulatovna Sharipova, Sarvar Temurovich Islomov, Nodira Isroilovna Tursunova, Sitora Rakhmatova, Fatima Shokir Qizi Shodieva, Mirzarakhim Mirzakhakimovich Baynazarov, Khasanjon Kobiljon Ugli Odilov, Dilbar Yuldashevna Yuldasheva, Goli
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCervical cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality among women in Uzbekistan, exceeding WHO elimination targets. Despite a school-based HPV vaccination program launched in 2019, screening coverage remains low, leading to delayed diagnoses; we examined cervical cancer trends in Tashkent (2014-2024) to evaluate the impact of the Korea Foundation for International Healthcare (KOFIH) screening project and UNFPA/UNDP HPV testing initiatives.MethodsWe analyzed Tashkent City Oncoregister data for women diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer or carcinoma in situ (CIS) between 2014 and

title: Comparative evaluation of pyrolysis oils derived from lignocellulosic biomass and municipal solid waste as potential bitumen modifiers
creator: Bhaswati Bora, Nikhil Saboo, Praveen Kumar, Sonal K. Thengane
description: The transition toward sustainable road construction has led to increased research on replacing conventional asphalt binders with bio-based and waste-derived alternatives. Bio-bitumen derived from lignocellulosic biomass and binders modified using domestic and industrial waste have shown significant potential in reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by up to 80%. Life cycle assessments have reported net-negative emissions for certain biomass-based binders.

title: Nitrogen fertilization outweighs plant species loss in shaping bacterial belowground diversity in an alpine meadow on the central Tibetan Plateau
creator: Dongmei Wu, CiRen Quzong, Zhongjun Jia, Antje Schwalb, Georg Guggenberger, Shiping Wang, Tsechoe Dorji, Michael Pester
description: Plant species loss and nitrogen fertilization affect grassland biodiversity. However, their interactive effects on plant communities, soil properties, and the soil microbiome remain insufficiently understood. We analysed how the removal of plant species, with and without urea addition, influenced plant diversity, soil properties, and soil bacterial communities in a Tibetan Plateau grassland.

title: Making Antibiotic Guidance Work in the Emergency Department
creator: Hae Suk Cheong
description: need more antibiotic knowledge [2]. Existing guidance is often designed in a form that does not match the work of emergency care [1,3]. The authors conducted focus group interviews with 16 physicians involved in antibiotic prescribing at four tertiary hospitals in Korea.

title: Bacteriophage-Antibiotic Combinations in the Era of Antimicrobial Resistance
creator: Shinwon Lee
description: es carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales among the critical-priority pathogens for research and development, together with other major resistant organisms that continue to threaten contemporary clinical practice [1]. Against this background, bacteriophage (or phage) therapy has re-emerged as a potential therapeutic option for difficult-to-treat bacterial infections, including those for which effective antibiotic options are limited, and as an adjunct to conventional therapy.

title: Synergistic Effect of Bacteriophage vB_KpnS_Pey and Antibiotic Combinations against Clinical Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolates
creator: Parva Farmehr, Salehe Sabouri, Roya Ahmadrajabi, Saereh Mohammadpour, Hossein Hosseini-Nave, Sanaz Rastegar
description: BackgroundThe global rise of antimicrobial resistance, particularly among carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP), presents a serious therapeutic challenge. This study aimed to isolate and characterize a bacteriophage effective against prophage-free CRKP and to evaluate its potential synergistic effects with ciprofloxacin, meropenem, gentamicin, and colistin.

title: Integrated RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies NRXN1+ Cell-Fibroblast Associated MAPK Signaling in Prurigo Nodularis
creator: Jiyun Jang, Young-Bok Lee, Hwee-Seon Park, Narang Hong, Hyung Don Kook, Hye Jung Jung, Jong-Il Kim, Jiyoung Ahn
description: PurposePrurigo nodularis (PN) is chronic pruritic dermatosis with hyperkeratotic nodules and persistent itch, occurring alone or with atopic dermatitis (AD). The molecular basis of nodular architecture and sustained pruritus remain poorly defined, particularly the role of fibroblasts and their interactions with neuronal components.

title: Association Between C-Reactive Protein-Triglyceride Glucose Index and All-Cause Mortality and Exacerbation in Adult Asthma: NHANES, 1999–2010 and 2015–2018
creator: Jiaye Wang, Miaomiao Zhao, Hao Chen, Shiyu Hu, Chengshui Chen, Yingqing Zhang, Wenyu Chen
description: PurposeThis study investigates the association between the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI), indicative of systemic inflammation and insulin resistance, and all-cause mortality as well as asthma exacerbations in adults with asthma.MethodsData from eight cycles of the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (1999–2010 and 2015–2018) were analyzed.

title: Psychotropic drugs in drinking water? A scoping review of evidence on diazepam and fluoxetine
creator: Paula Pinheiro Teixeira, Beatriz Assunção Pereira, Roberta da Silva Carneiro, Lara Júlia Moraes de Assis, Mariana Luiza Leal, Matheus Marcon
description: The global prevalence of mental disorders has increased considerably in recent decades. This evidence, associated with population growth and the expansion of access to medications, favors the growing global consumption of psychotropic drugs. Consequently, an increasing load of these substances is introduced into the environment, especially into water bodies, characterizing them as emerging contaminants.

title: Invasive alien plants in riparian ecosystems: a study from two lowland rivers in Eastern Poland
creator: Joanna Sender, Monika Różańska-Boczula
description: Riparian ecosystems are biodiversity hotspots but are also highly vulnerable to biological invasions due to strong hydrological connectivity, recurrent disturbance and exposure to nutrient inputs. This study examined patterns of invasive alien plant species (IAS) occurrence along two lowland rivers in eastern Poland (the Biala Lada and Czarna Lada).

title: InstructPLM-mu: protein fitness prediction from structure instructions
creator: Junde Xu, Yapin Shi, Lijun Lang, Taoyong Cui, Zhiming Zhang, Guangyong Chen, Jiezhong Qiu, Pheng-Ann Heng
description: Multimodal protein language models (PLMs) deliver strong performance on mutation-effect prediction, but training such models from scratch demands substantial computational resources. In this paper, we propose a fine-tuning framework called InstructPLM-mu and investigate the question: Can a pretrained sequence-only PLM, augmented with structural information during fine-tuning, match the performance of end-to-end trained multimodal models?

title: Therapeutic vaccines for NSCLC: From mechanisms to clinical translation
creator: Weijing Liu, Jiefei Han, Kailun Fei, Yiting Dong, Man Li, Jie Zhao, Mingzhao Wang, Zhuoran Li, Siyuan Chen, Jiachen Xu, Amit Jain
description: Despite advances in targeted therapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), durable disease control remains elusive for most patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), particularly those with advanced-stage disease. Therapeutic cancer vaccines offer the potential for sustained immune surveillance by inducing tumor-specific effector and memory T-cell responses. However, their clinical benefits have been inconsistent to date.

title: GDF-15 and immune resistance: A new frontier in non-small cell lung cancer immunotherapy
creator: Jun Lu, Hua Zhong, Baohui Han
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). notherapies represent two of the most critical challenges in oncology today. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for approximately 85% of all lung cancer cases, and in this setting, the challenge of immune resistance is particularly acute. Although multiple immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have been approved as standard-of-care therapies, a substantial proportion of patients either fail to respond initially or eventually acquire resistance. This underscores an urgent unmet need for novel therapeutic strategies in this prevalent malignancy.

title: Prevalence of anxiety and depression and diagnostic utility of the CAT scale in spirometry-confirmed COPD patients: Findings from the Chinese Population Health and Multimorbidities Study
creator: Sinan Wu, Jian Kang, Xiangyan Zhang, Lan Yang, Fuqiang Wen, Yuanlin Song, Jianping Zhao, Jianying Xu, Wen Li, Pixin Ran, Kewu Huang, Yahong Chen, Yanfei Guo, Guangliang Shan, Ting Yang, Chen Wang, Jieping Lei, Chinese Population Health and Multimorbidities Study (CPHMS) Investigators
description: BackgroundPatients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) frequently present with psychological comorbidities, including anxiety and depression, which may contribute to poorer clinical outcomes. However, the prevalence and impact of these mental health conditions in COPD patients have long been underrecognized.

title: Respiratory immunology: an ancient yet emerging interdisciplinary field
creator: Yuqing Lv, Weining Xiong, Bin Cao
description: also as a highly specialized barrier surface that integrates immune surveillance, inflammatory control, epithelial protection, and tissue repair.1,2 Tissue-resident immune cells, epithelial cells, stromal cells, and soluble mediators together maintain a dynamic equilibrium between host defense and immune tolerance at this environmental interface.

title: Roles of orexinergic and noradrenergic neuronal activity in ketamine-induced analgesia: A study using an orexin/ataxin-3 transgenic rat model
creator: Mitsuru Tonosaki, Tetsuya Kushikata, Yoshikazu Nikaido, Daiki Takekawa, Hirotaka Kinoshita, Jyunichi Saito, Kazuyoshi Hirota
description: BackgroundOrexin, a neuropeptide, physiologically interacts with locus coeruleus noradrenergic (LC-NA) activity. We hypothesized that this interaction affects ketamine-induced acute analgesia.MethodsWe assessed ketamine-induced acute analgesia in transgenic (TG) and wild-type (WT) rats with genetically degraded orexinergic neurons using hotplate and tail-flick tests.

title: Obturator hernia misdiagnosed as inguinal incarceration: a case of postoperative small-bowel perforation and subcutaneous fecal emphysema
creator: Anas Derkaoui, Tarik Deflaoui, Intissar Aissi, Abdelali Guellil, Rachid Jabi, Mohammed Bouziane
description: Introduction and importance:An obturator hernia is a rare condition accounting for less than 1% of abdominal wall hernias. Due to its deep pelvic location and nonspecific clinical presentation, it is frequently misdiagnosed, most often as an inguinal hernia. Delayed or incorrect diagnosis may result in bowel ischemia and perforation.

title: Can artificial intelligence-derived bone mineral density outperform traditional morphometric measurements in opportunistic osteoporosis screening using pelvic radiographs? A multicenter comparative diagnostic study
creator: Chia-Che Lee, Xi-Qian Heng, Hung-Kuan Yen, I-Hsin Chen, Tzu-Hao Tseng, Hong-Da Lu, Hung-Chun Lee, Ruey-Feng Chang, Chen-Yu Wang, Shau-Huai Fu
description: ObjectivesTo investigate whether an artificial intelligence (AI) model could demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy in identifying dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) confirmed osteoporosis, outperform traditional human-read metrics, and deliver substantial clinical net benefit.MethodsThis retrospective multicenter cohort study included 382 patients with hip fractures who had both preoperative pelvic radiographs and postoperative DXA scans.

title: Suppression of Elastic Scattering of CH4 by Graphene Passivation of Ni(111)
creator: Amjad Al Taleb, Francesc Viñes, Daniel Farías
description: We report high-resolution angular diffraction measurements of CH4 and Ne from Ni(111) and from a graphene (Gr) layer grown on Ni(111), whose effective atomic mass is enhanced by the strong Gr–Ni interaction. The incident energies are between 43 and 68 meV for Ne, and between 62 and 108 meV for CH4 beams.

title: Fall risk in rheumatoid arthritis revisited: A follow-up study focusing on sarcopenia and glucocorticoid use
creator: Naoki Nakagawa, Keita Nagira, Masako Hayashibara, Takashi Wada, Yuki Kitsuda, Yuta Takasu, Chikako Takeda, Mari Osaki, Hiroshi Hagino, Hideki Nagashima
description: ObjectivesTo re-evaluate fall incidence and its determinants in a contemporary cohort of ambulatory women with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in a follow-up study based on our previously published cohort data.MethodsWe prospectively evaluated 124 ambulatory female patients aged ≥50 years with RA at a single institution in 2022–2023, monitoring falls for 1 year.

title: Change in the life expectancy gap among people with mental illness: a 14-year population-based cohort study in Australia
creator: Mike Trott, David Lawrence, Sean Halstead, Claudia Bull, Dan Siskind, Steve Kisely
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBackgroundPeople with psychiatric disorders die substantially earlier than the general population, with life expectancy gaps of 10–20 years reported internationally. Prior Australian data indicated this gap was widening, whereas evidence from other countries has been mixed.

title: Descriptor: Synthetic Genomic Dataset With Diverse Ancestry (SynGen6)
creator: XINYUE WANG, SITAO MIN, JAIDEEP VAIDYA
description: Advancements in genomic analysis techniques and data-driven research are driving precision medicine. However, in many cases, these advances are not equitable and do not help all subpopulations, since many existing genomic datasets lack diversity, limiting their applicability for studying populations beyond those of European ancestry.

title: iProDNet: integrated probabilistic differential network inference under heterogeneous biological conditions
creator: Heewon Park, Seiya Imoto
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Understanding phenotype-specific network rewiring is essential for elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying complex diseases. Although numerous differential network analysis methods have been developed, most focus on only a limited aspect of network information. Consequently, these approaches often fail to jointly characterize regulatory activity and network architecture, provide limited statistical evidence at the network level, and offer little capability for prioritizing key genes that drive phenotype-specific network rewiring.

title: MHCXGraph: a graph-based approach to detecting T-cell receptor cross-reactivity
creator: Carlos D M S Simões, Rocío L B R Maidana, Samuel C de Assis, João V S Guerra, Helder V Ribeiro-Filho
description: The T-cell receptor (TCR) recognition of multiple peptides presented by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) is a key natural phenomenon, enabling the T-cell repertoire to respond to a broad array of antigens. Despite its importance to the immune response, T-cell cross-reactivity poses a major challenge for the development of novel T cell–based therapies.

title: PEARL: novel protein targets recommendation model via heterogeneous graph representation learning
creator: Zixuan Liu, Jiasi Luan, Zhen Zhang, Kui Tang, Xingyu Qin, Zhixiao Qi, Borui Zhang, Jun Liao
description: Peptide drug repurposing depends on identifying likely protein targets for a query peptide across a large candidate space, yet most existing peptide–protein interaction models are optimized for isolated pairwise classification rather than target prioritization. Here, we present PEARL, a recommendation-oriented heterogeneous graph learning framework for peptide target recommendation.

title: The Pathologic Roles and Therapeutic Implications of Ghrelin/GHSR System in Mental Disorders
creator: Qianshuo Mao, Jinjia Wang, Zihan Yang, Ruidong Ding, Shuangyu Lv, Xinying Ji
description: Ghrelin is a hormone consisting of 28 amino acids. Growth hormone secretagogue receptor (GHSR) is a receptor for ghrelin, which is expressed in the brain, pituitary gland, and adrenal glands, especially in the hypothalamus. The binding of ghrelin to the receptor 1a subtype mediates most of the biological effects of ghrelin.

title: Unsupervised identification of low-frequency antigen-specific TCRs using distance-based anomaly scoring
creator: Kyohei Kinoshita, Tetsuya J Kobayashi
description: Identifying antigen-specific T cell receptors (TCRs) within the diverse human repertoire remains challenging, particularly for low-frequency clonotypes. Here, we present TCR-RADAR (TCR Rare Antigen-specific Detection by Anomaly Ranking), an unsupervised approach that detects low-frequency antigen-specific TCRs through distance-based anomaly detection in TCR sequence space.

title: Cardiac magnetic resonance T1 mapping predicts outcome in patients with a systemic right ventricle: a sub-analysis of the SERVE study
creator: Odile Burdet, Kerstin Wustmann, Barbara E U Burkhardt, Emanuela R Valsangiacomo Buechel, Jean-Paul Vallée, Judith Bouchardy, Matthias Greutmann, Markus Schwerzmann, Harald Gabriel, Dominik Stambach, Daniel Tobler, Juerg Schwitter, Tobias Rutz, Annette Schophuus Jensen
description: AimsIn patients with a systemic right ventricle (sRV), the sRV is faced with an increased afterload compared to a right ventricle in sub-pulmonary position, leading to the development of fibrosis followed by ventricular dysfunction. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) T1 mapping (T1) and its derived parameter, such as the extracellular volume (ECV), allow quantification of interstitial fibrosis.

title: Endoscopic Management of Recurrent Biliary Sepsis Associated with Prolonged Biliary Stent Exposure into the Duodenal Bulb and Concurrent Duodenal Obstruction in Advanced Pancreatic Cancer

creator: Serena W Y Chong, Sarah Paulin, Faraz Khalid, Stephan Stenmark, Danilo Lo Fo Wong, Deborah Tong, Ketevan Kandelaki, Viroj Tangcharoensathien, Bassem Zayed, Abzal Zhumagaliuly, Erica Barbazza, Shamsuzzoha B Syed, Nienke Bruinsma

Primary care and the community serve as the frontlines for preventing and managing infections and addressing the rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

creator: Chudan Liang, Zequn Wang, Linjin Fan, Yulong Wang, Yuandong Zhou, Xiaofeng Yang, Jingyan Lin, Pengfei Ye, Wendi Shi, Hongxin Huang, Huijun Yan, Linna Liu, Jun Qian

There is an urgent demand to determine whether rapid quantification methods can accurately indicate intact viral infectivity in a shorter time for practical applications.

title: Motility-mediated drug interactions with GLP-1 receptor agonists: labeled evidence and a framework for quantitative assessment
creator: Jae Yong Chung
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely prescribed, and two additional oral products received US approval in 2025 and 2026. All eleven US labels examined describe delayed gastric emptying as potentially affecting the absorption of co-administered oral medications. Since the exenatide program, no study has evaluated a narrow therapeutic index victim across more than one administration schedule; the original warfarin and digoxin studies each used a single schedule. The omission may reflect an interaction paradigm built around enzymes and transporters.

creator: Philipp Krisai, Mikko Mutti, Stefanie Aeschbacher, Michael Coslovsky, Tobias Reichlin, Nicolas Rodondi, Peter Ammann, Giorgio Moschovitis, Elia Rigamonti, Giulio Conte, Moa L Haller, Amelie Stoecklin, Leo H Bonati, Stefan Osswald, David Conen, Felix Mahfoud, Michael Kühne

We aimed to investigate the prevalence of eGFRdiff and its association with clinical outcomes and brain lesions in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).Methods and resultsWe analysed 3804 patients with AF enrolled in two prospective, multicentre cohort studies.

title: Liquid biopsy in gallbladder carcinoma: Current evidence and future prospective
creator: Sridhar Mishra, Swati Kumari, Nuzhat Husain
description: Although there have been significant advances in the early detection and treatment of gallbladder cancer (GBC), it is still considered a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. Molecular profiling of tumors is generally performed using samples obtained during surgery or biopsy.

title: Experiences of school health professionals in implementing structured assessments of sexual health and experiences of violence among youth in Sweden using the SEXual health Identification Tool (SEXIT): a qualitative sequential study
creator: Miranda Håkansson, Sanny Söderström, Marlene Makenzius
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionPoor sexual and reproductive health (SRH) is a global public health concern, particularly among adolescents. While school health services (SHS) play a crucial role in preventative care, professionals are inconsistent in addressing SRH issues.

title: Steroids and Malignancy Increase Local Heparanase and Decrease Markers of Osteoblast Activity in Bone Tissue Microcirculation
creator: Keren Asayag, Eli Peled, Mai Assalia, Yonatan Crispel, Chen Yanovich, Haim Cohen, Anat Keren-Politansky, Yona Nadir, Masaru Yamaguchi, Peixin Dong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Bone metastasis and steroids are known to activate the coagulation system and induce osteoporosis, pathological bone fractures, and bone pain. Heparanase is a protein known to enhance the hemostatic system and to promote angiogenesis, metastasis, and inflammation. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the effects of steroids and malignancy on the coagulation factors and osteoblast activity in the bone tissue.

title: Synthesis and Characterization of Two Sparfloxacin Crystalline Salts: Enhancing Solubility and In Vitro Antibacterial Activity of Sparfloxacin
creator: Wei Sun, Ruili Huo, Jingzhong Duan, Jixiang Xiao, Yan Wang, Xiaoping Zhou, Clive Prestidge
description: Background: To improve the solubility and permeability of Sparfloxacin (SPX) and enhance its antimicrobial activity in vitro, two unreported pharmaceutical crystalline salts were synthesized and characterized in this paper. One is a hydrated crystal of Sparfloxacin with Pimelic acid (PIA), another is a hydrated crystal of Sparfloxacin with Azelaic acid (AZA), namely, SPX-PIA-H2O (2C19H23F2N4O3·C7H10O4·2H2O) and SPX-AZA-H2O (4C19H23F2N4O3·2C9H14O4·5H2O).

title: Comparison of Phacoemulsification and Aspiration Parameters in Cataract Surgery: Metal Tip vs. Hybrid Tip
creator: Kazuo Ichikawa, Kei Ichikawa, Seiji Tokiwa, Yuki Sato, Tomoyuki Miyazaki, Yoshiki Tanaka, Naoki Yamamoto, Jianxing Ma, Dimitrios Karamichos
description: Various tips are available for phacoemulsification in cataract surgery. Evidence-based data can inform ophthalmologists, especially inexperienced ones, on tip selection. We retrospectively evaluated the energy efficiency and other parameters of two ultrasonic phacoemulsification and aspiration tips across different nuclear hardness grades in 342 cataract patients (342 eyes) with nuclear hardness grades II to IV.

title: Comparison of Biocompatibility of 3D-Printed Ceramic and Titanium in Micropig Ankle Hemiarthroplasty
creator: Si-Wook Lee, Donghyun Lee, Junsik Kim, Sanghyun An, Chul-Hyun Park, Jung-Min Lee, Chang-Jin Yon, Yu-Ran Heo, Antonia Patruno, Teresa Paolucci, Mirko Pesce, Andrea Pantalone, Elisa Belluzzi

In addition to typical arthritis, there is also structural bone loss in the talus due to diseases such as talar avascular necrosis.

title: Quantum Circuit Architecture Search on a Superconducting Processor
creator: Kehuan Linghu, Yang Qian, Ruixia Wang, Meng-Jun Hu, Zhiyuan Li, Xuegang Li, Huikai Xu, Jingning Zhang, Teng Ma, Peng Zhao, Dong E Liu, Min-Hsiu Hsieh, Xingyao Wu, Yuxuan Du, Dacheng Tao, Yirong Jin, Haifeng Yu, Giuliano Benenti
description: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) have shown strong evidence to gain provable computational advantages in diverse fields such as finance, machine learning, and chemistry. However, the heuristic ansatz exploited in modern VQAs is incapable of balancing the trade-off between expressivity and trainability, which may lead to degraded performance when executed on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) machines.

title: SDR3.1 negatively regulates seed dormancy in Poaceae crops
creator: Naihui Guo, Ruihu An, Mengxue Xu, Yuanyuan Li, Zongliang Ren, Jun Jiang, Bonian Cai, Xinzhu Huang, Shikai Hu, Gaoneng Shao, Guiai Jiao, Lihong Xie, Ling Wang, Fengli Zhao, Yujun Zhu, Shaoqing Tang, Zhonghua Sheng, Peisong Hu
description: SUMMARYElucidating the molecular mechanisms that govern seed dormancy is important for developing crops with improved resistance to preharvest sprouting (PHS). A series of seed dormancy genes have been cloned, but the connections among different seed dormancy genes remain poorly understood. Here, we have revealed the relationship between two important dormancy quantitative trait loci (QTLs): SDR3.1 and Sdr4. SDR3.

title: Advancements and Challenges in the Management of Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis: A Review
creator: Francesco Nappi, Deborah Anderson
description: Prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) is the medical term used to describe a focus of infection involving a valvular substitute within the heart. It is a significant concern in the field of cardiology, and the epidemiology of PVE has seen notable developments over the last five decades.

title: Translation and comprehensive validation of the Neurological Outcome Scale for Traumatic Brain Injury (NOS-TBI) into Brazilian Portuguese
creator: Karina T. Weber, Luciana B. M. Alves, Monica C. Braga, Suleimy C. Mazin, Brunna R. Pileggi, Millene R. Camilo, Viviane A. Guimaraes, Clara M. A. Barreira, Frederico Alessio-Alves, Aline S. Carvalho, Aline C. Pacheco-Castilho, João P. Leite, Dylan J. Edwards, Octavio M. Pontes-Neto, Taiza G. S. Edwar
description: BackgroundTraumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of disability in Brazil and worldwide. National and multinational clinical trials in TBI require global standardization of outcome measures. The original English version of the Neurological Outcome Scale for TBI (NOS-TBI) is a valid and valuable neurological assessment tool. However, NOS-TBI has not yet been validated in Brazilian Portuguese.

title: Continuous frusemide infusion versus intermittent bolus therapy in paediatric intensive care: A single centre retrospective study
creator: Nutnicha Preeprem, Emily See, Siva P Namachivayam, Ben Gelbart
description: ObjectiveFrusemide is a common diuretic administered to critically ill children intravenously, by either continuous infusion (CI) or intermittent bolus (IB). We aim to describe the characteristics of children who receive intravenous frusemide, patterns of use, and incidence of acute kidney injury (AKI), and to investigate factors associated with commencing CI.DesignRetrospective observational study.

title: Laparoscopic and Robotic Appendectomy: Efficiency and Cost Comparison
creator: Madeleine T Dang, Shaanali Mukadam, Chang Kon Kim, Daniel H Choi, Timothy J Chu, Devendra K Agrawal
description: Acute appendicitis is a common cause of emergency abdominal surgery, most frequently affecting adolescents and young adults. Diagnosis is often complicated by variable clinical presentations, and timely recognition is critical to prevent complications such as perforation, peritonitis, and intra-abdominal abscess formation.

title: Analysis of Implementation Strategies for Nationwide HPV Vaccination Programs Across European Union Countries
creator: Wojciech Miazga, Tomasz Tatara, Mariusz Gujski, Janusz Ostrowski, Jarosław Pinkas, Urszula Religioni
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programs play a critical role in the primary prevention of HPV-related diseases, including cervical cancer. However, the principles governing the implementation of these programs vary across European Union (EU) countries. The objective of this study was to analyze and compare the strategies for implementing HPV vaccination programs across the EU, with a focus on access, vaccine selection, and procurement processes.

title: Polio Epidemiology: Strategies and Challenges for Polio Eradication Post the COVID-19 Pandemic
creator: Lucia F. Bricks, Denis Macina, Juan C. Vargas-Zambrano
description: The Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI), launched in 1988, has successfully reduced wild poliovirus (WPV) cases by over 99.9%, with WPV type 2 and WPV3 declared eradicated in 2015 and 2019, respectively. However, as of 2024, WPV1 remains endemic in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

title: Coumarins as modulators of protein–protein interactions: Computational insights, biological mechanisms, and translational perspectives
creator: Yasser Fakri Mustafa
description: Coumarins are versatile bioactive scaffolds capable of interacting with diverse biomolecules, yet their potential role in modulating protein–protein complexes remains insufficiently characterized. Modern computational biology now enables rational exploration of how small molecules can influence structural coupling, signal transduction, and pathway rewiring at the interface of proteins.

title: Predicting brain tumour enhancement from non-contrast MRI with artificial intelligence: a multicohort, retrospective, diagnostic accuracy study
creator: James K Ruffle, Samia Mohinta, Guilherme Pombo, Asthik Biswas, Alan Campbell, Indran Davagnanam, David Doig, Ahmed Hammam, Harpreet Hyare, Farrah Jabeen, Emma Lim, Dermot Mallon, Stephanie Owen, Sophie Wilkinson, Sebastian Brandner, Parashkev Nachev

title: CYP2D6 Metabolizer Status Does Not Predict Response or Tolerability of Low-Dose Nortriptyline for Irritable Bowel Syndrome With Diarrhea
creator: Kyle Staller, Jenna Clukey, Elizabeth N Madva, Brian C Healy, Minyi Lee, Manish K Gala

Genotype-inferred phenotype of CYP2D6 can classify patients into different metabolizer classes.5 Although genetic testing is widely available, it is unclear if these polymorphisms are relevant to the use of low-dose TCAs in IBS-D.

title: Dermal Scaffolds in Complex Extremity Wound Reconstruction: Impact of Early Application on Grafting and Flap Requirements—A Systematic Review
creator: Rania Darwish, Simon M. Kratzer, Deepak M. Kalaskar, Peter Butler, Suvashis Dash

This review evaluated whether early dermal scaffold application reduces subsequent surgical requirements. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library and clinical trial registries were searched for studies published between 2016 and 2026.

title: The Association Between Brominated Flame Retardants Exposure and Liver-Related Biomarkers in US Adults
creator: Yuqing Chen, Yulan Cheng, Jialing Ruan, Donglei Huang, Jing Xiao, Xinyuan Zhao, Jinlong Li, Jianhua Qu, Xiaoke Wang, Giovanna Tranfo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Emerging studies demonstrate that exposure to brominated flame retardants (BFRs) can have harmful effects on human health. Our study focused on the relationship between exposure to various BFRs and markers of liver function. Methods: To further explore the association between BFR exposure and liver function impairment, we used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Surveys (NHANES) for three cycles from 2009 to 2014, leaving 4206 participants (≥20 years of age) after screening.

title: Microbiology and antimicrobial resistance in biliary tract infections including acute and post-ERCP cholangitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis

creator: Ebtihal Elameen Eltyeb, Ali Ali Al-Makramani

title: Far‐Red Light Supplementation in Tomato Cultivation: A Quantitative Review of Morphological and Physiological Responses
creator: Anna Fischer, Irene Vänninen, Kristiina Himanen

Recently, research has focused on the effects of FR light on the growth and development of crops, like tomatoes.

title: Computational evaluation of novel Schiff base compounds targeting Mycobacterium tuberculosis

Key enzymes involved in mycobacterial cell wall biosynthesis, including DprE1, InhA, KasA, MmpL3, and LdtMt2, represent attractive therapeutic targets for anti-tubercular drug discovery.

Glutamic acid (GLA) is an amino acid that affects human metabolism. Since an anti-cancer mechanism of FQs is human topoisomerase II inhibition, it is expected that FQ-GLA hybrids can act similarly.

title: Biopsy-Proven Prostatic Metastasis From Diffuse-Type Gastric Adenocarcinoma Presenting With Bilateral Malignant Ureteric Obstruction: A Case Report

creator: Morgan Walker, Chris W Baugh

Hemolytic anemia results from either the intravascular or extravascular breakdown of red blood cells. The most common causes of secondary hemolytic anemia include lymphoproliferative disorders, autoimmune disorders, and infections.

title: Correlation of the FIB-4 Liver Biomarker Score with the Severity of Heart Failure
creator: Roxana Buzas, Paul Ciubotaru, Alexandra Corina Faur, Marius Preda, Melania Ardelean, Doina Georgescu, Patrick Dumitrescu, Daniel Florin Lighezan, Mihaela-Diana Popa, Petar Otašević

title: Synovial Fluid Markers and Extracellular Vesicles in Rheumatoid Arthritis

creator: Genevieve Perrins, Israt Jahan, Md. Nuruzzaman Khan, Mahmudul Hassan Al Imam, Rosalie Power, Catherine King, Mohammad Muhit, Nadia Badawi, Gulam Khandaker
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: Cerebral palsy (CP) affects a substantial number of children, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Bangladesh. In this study, we sought to assess how the mPower (mother’s power) community-based intervention impacted mothers’ CP-specific knowledge, as well as their utilization of rehabilitation services in rural Bangladesh.

creator: Babatope O. Adebiyi, Kathryn A. Birnie, Heinrike Schmeling
description: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) is a chronic autoimmune condition in children that often requires long-term pain management, which can include opioid use. We integrate energy–economy, coupled meteorology–chemistry, and photovoltaic performance models to quantify how alternative carbon-neutrality pathways influence solar power generation via air quality changes in China.

The Ponseti method has become the gold standard for clubfoot treatment, replacing previous extensive surgical approaches. However, there is a lack of prospective long-term data comparing surgical and Ponseti treatments.

Mucinous gastric adenocarcinoma (MGC) is a distinct histologic subtype characterized by poor prognosis and limited responsiveness to chemotherapy and immunotherapy. CRACD, an actin polymerization regulator, is frequently inactivated in gastric cancer (GC), with enrichment in mucinous subtypes. We found that genetic engineering of murine gastric organoids with Cracd ablation combined with Kras mutation and Trp53 loss induced mucinous cell plasticity, disrupted epithelial integrity, and promoted immune evasion.

The annual risk of hemorrhage is between 2–4%, with a mortality rate of 10%, and 50% of survivors may experience permanent neurological deficits.

In conventional Pt/C catalysts, differences between Pt and carbon surfaces promote sulfonate adsorption on Pt and ionomer aggregation on carbon, thereby limiting proton and oxygen transport.

title: Could CH3-M6P Be a Potential Dual-Functioning Candidate for Bone Regeneration?
creator: Fidan Huseynova, Cătălina Ionescu, Frederic Cuisinier, Irada Huseynova, Alamdar Mammadov, Véronique Barragan-Montero
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: CI-RM6P has different binding sites with affinities for both M6P and IGF2, plays a role in the regulation of the TGF-β and IGF pathways that is important for controlling cell growth and differentiation. We hypothesize that previously synthesised derivative of M6P could be an alternative candidate for bone tissue regeneration in terms of higher binding affinity, stability in human serum, low cost and temporal delivery.

title: Pectus Excavatum
creator: Krishnaswamy Chandrasekaran, Farouk Mookadam
description: Corresponding Author Pectus excavatum (PE) is usually not considered causative in adults presenting with cardiopulmonary symptoms despite a thorough cardiopulmonary evaluation by cardiologists and pulmonologists for disabling cardiopulmonary symptoms.1,2 Kragten et al1 developed a score for evaluating symptoms, the symptomatic pectus excavatum in seniors (SPES) score, and the magnitude of pectus compression, the pectus evaluation index score (PEI).

title: When the Flag Identifies the Territory But Not the Mechanism
creator: Tsuneaki Kenzaka
description: Corresponding Author Acute allergic coronary syndromes remain underrecognized, perhaps owing to their ability to mimic classic ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). In this issue of JACC: Case Reports, Deb et al1 describe a compelling case in which a patient developed severe chest pain and the South African Flag sign immediately after iodinated contrast administration.

title: Looking Beyond the Annulus
creator: Ana Paula Tagliari
description: Corresponding AuthorKey Words: aortic root anatomy, computed tomography, sinotubular junction, structural heart disease, transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) Since its introduction, transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has evolved from a procedure guided primarily by anatomical feasibility to one driven by anatomical precision.

title: Pharmacotherapy from Pre-COVID to Post-COVID: Longitudinal Trends and Predictive Indicators for Long COVID Symptoms
creator: Nadia Baalbaki, Sien T. Verbeek, Harm Jan Bogaard, Jelle M. Blankestijn, Vera C. van den Brink, Merel E. B. Cornelissen, Jos W. R. Twisk, Korneliusz Golebski, Anke H. Maitland-van der Zee
description: Background/objectives: A significant number of COVID-19 cases experience persistent symptoms after the acute infection phase, a condition known as long COVID or post-acute sequelae of COVID-19. Approved prevention and treatment options for long COVID are currently lacking. Given the heterogeneous nature of long COVID, a personalized medicine approach is essential for effective disease management.

title: Shifting Baseline of Continuous Thermodilution
creator: Pitt O Lim
description: xia during ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction increases infarct size,3 and older similar studies with intracoronary oxygen delivery showed neither obvious infarct size reduction, nor better outcome at 30 days.4 Looking critically at the report of Velazquez Gutierrez et al,1 the following 3 observations are pertinent: 1.

title: First Reported Native Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement in Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
creator: John T. D'Angelo, Karan Sud, Nikoloz Shekiladze, Joel T. Hardin, Nikoloz Koshkelashvili, Patrick T. Gleason, Adam B. Greenbaum, Vasilis C. Babaliaros
description: BackgroundCongenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries (CC-TGA) can lead to severe systemic tricuspid regurgitation (TR). There is limited evidence on transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) in these patients.Case SummaryA 59-year-old woman with CC-TGA presented with symptomatic severe systemic TR. She was at high risk for surgery, and transcatheter interventions were considered by our heart team.

title: Effective Coverage of Modern Contraceptive Use in Ethiopia: An Ecological Linking Analysis of Service Provision Assessment and National Health Equity Surveys
creator: Misrak Getnet, Samson Gebremedhin, Dessalegn Y Melesse, Melinda K Munos, Elizabeth A Hazel, Yohannes D Wado, Arega Zeru, Alemayehu Worku, Ndola Prata
description: The increase in contraceptive prevalence rate (crude coverage) in Ethiopia over the past two decades does not necessarily reflect service quality, and although the proportion of women with unmet needs has decreased, it remains unacceptably high. Hence, this study aimed to estimate the effective coverage (EC) of modern contraceptive methods in Ethiopia, considering the quality of care.

title: A case of human trombiculosis caused by Eutrombicula alfreddugesi (Acariformes: Prostigmata: Trombiculidae) in Chamela, Jalisco, Mexico
creator: Ricardo Paredes-León, Carmen Guzmán-Cornejo, Risa Pesapane
description: A case of trombiculosis is presented at the Estación de Biología Chamela in Jalisco, Mexico. This occurred during an expedition in search of parasites in the fall of 2024. One of the participants presented small red macules on her shins and ankles, and when these were observed with a portable magnifying glass, the presence of chiggers (Trombiculidae) was confirmed.

title: Improvements to pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity, Ethiopia
creator: Kedir Tahir Hagos, Tsige Gebre-Mariam, David Woo, Abraham Gebregiorgis Kahsay, Mengistab Woldearegay Teferi, Jicui Dong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ProblemEthiopia's heavy dependence on imported pharmaceuticals created public health vulnerabilities, foreign exchange pressures and recurrent medicine stock-outs.ApproachIn 2015, Ethiopia launched a 10-year National Strategy and Plan of Action for Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Development to improve access to quality-assured medicines. The strategy, overseen by a Joint Steering Committee co-chaired by the Ministries of Health and Industry with technical assistance from the World Health Organization (WHO), combined industrial incentives, preferential centralized procurement and regulatory strengthening.Local settingBefore strategy implementation, Ethiopia had limited manufacturing capacity.

title: Association Between Chronic Pain and Fatigue Severity with Weather and Air Pollution Among Females with Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS)
creator: Chloe Lisette Jones, Olivia Haskin, Jarred Wayne Younger, Megan L Benka-Coker
description: Weather and air quality conditions have been anecdotally reported to be related to symptom fluctuations in Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS), but this has never been empirically investigated. This exploratory study aims to examine the effects of weather and air quality on daily fluctuations of chronic pain and fatigue in women with ME/CFS.

title: Epistemic injustice in climate health research
creator: Verina Wild, Anthony Capon, Jan-Christoph Heilinger, Cristian Timmermann, Mujahid Torwali, Jakelin Troy
description: f knowledge production, validation and exchange.4 The harmful effects of these injustices are well documented, for instance in gender medicine, health research from low- and middle-income countries or in relation to traditional medicine.5,6 The concept of epistemic injustice is useful in understanding the structural origin and extent of imbalances in knowledge production.

title: Phase III AIRTIVITY study design: verducatib (BI 1291583) in people with bronchiectasis
creator: James D. Chalmers, Michal Shteinberg, Sanjay H. Chotirmall, Wiebke Sauter, Patrick A. Flume, Raksha Jain, Kozo Morimoto, Anne E. O'Donnell, Felix C. Ringshausen, Henrik Watz, Jin-Fu Xu, Johanna Rauch, Anastasia Eleftheraki, Annemarie T. Engel, Anne B. Chang, Kim G. Nielsen, Giselle Benitez, Abhya Gu
description: Graphical abstract Overview of the key elements of the AIRTIVITY study design. CatC: cathepsin C; CatG: cathepsin G; CF: cystic fibrosis; DPP1: dipeptidyl peptidase 1; NE: neutrophil elastase; NSP: neutrophil serine protease; PEx: pulmonary exacerbation; PR3: proteinase 3; SGRQ: St George's Respiratory Questionnaire. #: Requiring antibiotic treatment.

title: Coupling Up: A Dynamic Investigation of Romantic Partners’ Neurobiological States During Nonverbal Connection
creator: Cailee M. Nelson, Christian O’Reilly, Mengya Xia, Caitlin M. Hudac
description: Nonverbal connection is an important aspect of everyday communication. For romantic partners, nonverbal connection is essential for establishing and maintaining feelings of closeness. EEG hyperscanning offers a unique opportunity to examine the link between nonverbal connection and neural synchrony among romantic partners.

title: Optimizing Curriculum Integration: Development and Validation of the Tool of Integration Practices (TIP) in Health Professions Education - A Mixed Methods Study
creator: Syeda Rabbab Hasan, Madiha Sajjad, Rehan Ahmed Khan
description: Objective:Curriculum integration is increasingly adopted in medical and dental education, yet only a few validated tools exist to measure it objectively. Existing curriculum integration frameworks, including Harden’s ladder, are primarily descriptive and challenging to apply for systematic evaluation. Therefore, this study aimed to develop a valid and reliable tool to assess the level of integration in medical and dental curricula.

title: Metachromatic Leukodystrophy in Morocco: Identification of Causative Variants by Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)
creator: Miloud Hammoud, María Domínguez-Ruiz, Imane Assiri, Daniel Rodrigues, Nisrine Aboussair, Val F. Lanza, Jesús Villarrubia, Cristóbal Colón, Naima Fdil, Francisco J. del Castillo
description: (1) Background: Most rare disease patients endure long delays in obtaining a correct diagnosis, the so-called “diagnostic odyssey”, due to a combination of the rarity of their disorder and the lack of awareness of rare diseases among both primary care professionals and specialists.

title: Response–Response Binding: New Evidence from Event-Related Potentials Data
creator: Biye Wang, Lu Wang, Tao Tao, Wei Guo
description: Background: Response–response (RR) binding, involving the integration of independently planned and executed responses, presents a novel perspective on action control. While behavioral evidence on RR binding has been extensively examined, corresponding electrophysiological evidence remains scarce. This study aims to contribute novel insights into RR binding by event-related potentials (ERP) techniques to provide new evidence for RR binding.

title: Diagnostic Value of ANA Titer, Anti-ds-DNA, Anti-nRNPSm, and Sm Antibodies in Early Atypical Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
creator: Jianqiao Zhang, Meichen Liu, Qing Liu, Dong Chen, Meng Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objective:To explore the diagnostic value of antinuclear antibody(ANA) titer, anti-double-stranded DNA(anti-ds-DNA) antibody, anti-nuclear ribonucleoprotein/Smith(anti-nRNPSm) antibody, and Smith (Sm) antibody for early atypical systemic lupus erythematosus(SLE).Methodology:This was a retrospective study. Forty-nine patients diagnosed with early atypical SLE admitted to Affiliated Hospital of Hebei University between January 2023 to June 2025 were assigned to Group-A, and 66 patients with other autoimmune diseases admitted during the same period were enrolled in Group-B.

title: Urolithin A Protects Hepatocytes from Palmitic Acid-Induced ER Stress by Regulating Calcium Homeostasis in the MAM
creator: Gayoung Ryu, Minjeong Ko, Sooyeon Lee, Se In Park, Jin-Woong Choi, Ju Yeon Lee, Jin Young Kim, Ho Jeong Kwon, Alessandro Alaimo
description: An ellagitannin-derived metabolite, Urolithin A (UA), has emerged as a potential therapeutic agent for metabolic disorders due to its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and mitochondrial function-improving properties, but its efficacy in protecting against ER stress remains underexplored. The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a cellular organelle involved in protein folding, lipid synthesis, and calcium regulation.

title: Effect of Blood Orange (Citrus sinensis L. Osbeck) Peel Waste as a Feed Additive on the Growth Performance, Digestive Enzyme Activity, Antioxidant Capacity, and Immune Response in Juvenile Black Rockfish (Sebastes schlegelii)
creator: Tae Hoon Lee, Ki-Tae Kim, Hwa Yong Oh, Seo Young Park, Gyu Jin Lee, Hyun-Soo Kim, Hee Sung Kim, Inês Guerreiro
description: This study evaluated bioactive compounds in blood orange (Citrus sinensis (L.) Osbeck) peel (BOP) as dietary additives. An 8-week feeding trial was conducted to investigate the effects of dietary supplementation on the growth performance, body composition, digestive enzyme activity, antioxidant capacity, and immune response of juvenile black rockfish. A total of 1260 juvenile rockfish (1.4 ± 0.

title: Correlation between Prenatal Fetal Hemodynamic Parameters and Growth Indices in Pregnant Women with Preeclampsia and Neonatal Ultrasound Indicators of Organ Development
creator: Shudan Yin, Jianhong Wang, Jinying Liu
description: Objectives:This retrospective study aimed to explore the associations between prenatal fetal hemodynamics and growth parameters in pregnant women with preeclampsia and neonatal ultrasound assessment indicators of organ development.Methodology:Clinical parameters of 296 pregnant women and their neonates admitted to Xi’an Fourth Hospital from December 2024 to December 2025 were collected.

title: Glycaemic trends, trajectories and control during TB treatment and its association with TB treatment outcome among patients with TB–diabetes multimorbidity
creator: Maham Zahid, Mahmoud Danaee, Saima Aleem, Saima Afaq
description: Objectives:This study aimed to examine longitudinal glycaemic patterns, including trends, trajectories, and control during TB treatment, and their association with treatment outcomes in patients with Tuberculosis (TB) diabetes multimorbidity.Methodology:Analytical cross-sectional study was conducted, involving secondary analysis of an implementation study conducted at 13 Tuberculosis clinics in KPK and Punjab from June 2022 to June 2025.

title: Differences in Physiological and Agronomic Traits and Evaluation of Adaptation of Seven Maize Varieties
creator: Shuqi Ding, Dan Zhang, Ying Hao, Mengting Hu, Huijuan Tian, Kaizhi Yang, Guolong Zhao, Ruohang Xu, Wentao Du, Juwu Gong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryIn order to understand and utilize the adaptability of different maize varieties in the Alar region of Southern Xinjiang, 19 agronomic and physiological traits were measured using seven maize varieties as experimental materials.

title: Carbetocin versus oxytocin during elective cesarean delivery: A randomized double-blind trial
creator: Baran Tureli, Nurettin Kurt, Erbil Karaman, Nureddin Yuzkat
description: Objective:Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) remains a leading cause of maternal morbidity following cesarean delivery. This study aimed to compare the effects of carbetocin and oxytocin on intraoperative blood loss during elective cesarean delivery, with secondary evaluation of uterine tone, additional uterotonic requirements, and intraoperative hemodynamic parameters.

title: Biofluid-Derived Exosomal LncRNAs: Their Potential in Obesity and Related Comorbidities
creator: Ebenezeri Erasto Ngowi, Tuyan Lu, Qing Liu, Xianghong Xie, Ning Wang, Liping Luo, Lijuan Deng, Yinghua Zhou, Zhihong Zhang, Aijun Qiao, Natalia Cuesta
description: Simple SummaryExosomal cargo serves as a crucial mediator of cell-to-cell communication. The evidence suggests that exosomal long non-coding (exo-lncRNAs) are altered in the biofluids (such as blood, vitreous humor, and tears) of patients with metabolic disorders and correlate with key metabolic parameters, including body mass index, inflammation, and insulin sensitivity.

title: Digital delivery of the GDS method for chronic lumbosacral discogenic pain: A pilot study aligning Sustainable development Goals three and four
creator: Haroon Mansha, Saleh Shah, Muhammad Naveed Babur, Muhammad Junaid Ijaz
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and Objectives:A person’s quality of life and everyday functioning may be significantly restricted by chronic back pain including lumbosacral discogenic pain. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the GDS method’s initial effects on patients with chronic lumbosacral discogenic pain in terms of both pain and quality of life delivered through a smart phone application in a pilot study.Methodology:Between July 2025 and September 2025, a one-group pretest-posttest design was chosen, and a total of fifteen patients (six male and nine

title: Efficacy of lenvatinib combined with sintilimab and transcatheter arterial chemoembolization in conversion therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Jianwu Long, Jinli Zheng, Shiyi Chen, Peng Ou, Xianzhou Lu
description: Objectives:To compare the efficacy of lenvatinib combined with sintilimab versus transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) in the conversion therapy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).Methodology:A retrospective analysis of the clinical data of 153 patients with unresectable HCC admitted to the Affiliated Hospital of Nanhua University from January 2023 to December 2024 was performed.

title: Successful Fertility Preservation in a Case of Low-Grade Endometrial Stromal Sarcoma: A Multidisciplinary Approach Through the Oncofertility Network
creator: Katsuhiro Ooi, Yu Wakimoto, Noriyoshi Oki, Mina Sakata, Seiji Mabuchi
description: Low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma (LGESS) is a rare disease, accounting for less than 1% of all uterine malignancies. Standard treatment is total hysterectomy and bilateral tubal oophorectomy, although fertility preservation may be desirable because of the young age of onset.

title: Right Ventricular Myxoma Involving the Chordae Tendineae: A Case Report and Literature Review
creator: Rishab Makam, Ayush Balaji, Akshay Balaji, Ramanish Ravishankar, Natasha Bocchetta, Mohamed Sherif, Mahmoud Loubani
description: This case report describes a rare instance of massive right ventricular myxoma (RVM). A 36-year-old woman initially presented with progressive breathlessness and chest heaviness. Imaging revealed a large mass in the mediastinum, which was initially thought to be a pericardial cyst, and it was unclear whether the mass was intracardiac or extracardiac.

title: A dual-host regulatory hub integrating biofilm formation and innate immunity resistance
creator: Alexandre Baillez, Amélie Dewitte, François Pierre, Mounia Kortebi, Virginia S. Lioy, Mélanie Hillion, Julie Hardouin, Sébastien Janel, Xavier Thuru, Charlotte Clarisse, Hassiba Bouafia, Catherine Robbe Masselot, Sébastien Bontemps-Gallo, Florent Sebbane
description: Vector-borne pathogens must adapt to sharply distinct host environments, yet the regulatory logic that coordinates transitions between opposing host-specific programs remains poorly defined. Here, we identify a minimal regulatory module in the flea-borne pathogen Yersinia pestis that integrates vector transmission with resistance to mammalian innate immunity.

title: Efficacy of Supratherapeutic Duloxetine Combined With Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy in Severe Treatment-Resistant Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder With Comorbid Depression: A Case Report
creator: Syed Ali Bokhari, Mohamed H Nasr, Yasmeen T Alawadhi
description: This case report discusses the treatment of a 42-year-old male with over a decade of treatment-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and comorbid major depressive disorder (MDD). The patient underwent various pharmacological and psychotherapeutic treatments, including multiple antidepressants and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), yet experienced only partial symptom relief.

title: Submolecular video-imaging of the Smc5/6 complex topologically bound to DNA
creator: Kenichi Umeda, Yumiko Kurokawa, Noriyuki Kodera, Yasuto Murayama
description: Structural maintenance of chromosomes (SMC) complexes, including cohesin and condensin, are ring-shaped ATPases that organize chromosome architecture by holding DNA segments together. However, the dynamic mechanisms underlying their DNA binding and processing remain unclear. Using high-speed atomic force microscopy, we directly visualized the eukaryotic Smc5/6 complex on DNA at submolecular resolution.

title: Attachment Styles in Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
creator: Lingfeng Xue, Virginia Chi Tong Chau, Anokhi Mehra, Rachel Woodham, Gabrielle Sheehan, Valentina Lorenzetti, Michal W. S. Ong, Muzzammil Hussain, Anna J. Lawes, Ramesh Muthuswamy, Cynthia H. Y. Fu
description: Major depressive disorder (MDD), a leading cause of disability, is associated with difficulties in close relationships. Attachment theory links early caregiving to internal working models shaping emotion regulation, interpersonal functioning and depression vulnerability. Attachment patterns in clinically diagnosed MDD have not been synthesised.

title: European EHBP1L1 Genotyping Survey of Dyserythropoietic Anemia and Myopathy Syndrome in English Springer Spaniels
creator: Sarah Østergård Jensen, Alexandra Kehl, Urs Giger, J Alberto Montoya-Alonso
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryA syndromic hereditary disorder known as dyserythropoietic anemia and myopathy syndrome (DAMS) with perinatal losses was recently described, from its clinical signs to the discovered gene identification and mutation, in English Springer Spaniel dogs from Sweden and Australia. The disorder is characterized by defective red blood and muscle cells, leading to anemia and muscle wasting, with affected dogs having progressive illness including difficulty moving, drinking, and eating.

title: First Evidence of Cotinine in Canine Semen Reveals Tobacco Smoke Exposure
creator: Debora Groppetti, Giulia Pizzi, Elisa Giussani, Alessandro Pecile, Silvia Michela Mazzola, Valerio Bronzo, Eleonora Fusi, Xueming Zhang
description: Simple SummaryIn men, cigarette components have been shown to cross the blood–testis barrier, as they are detectable in the ejaculate of both active and passive smokers. However, no such data exist for dogs. To fill this gap, we investigated the presence of cotinine—a biomarker of nicotine exposure—in the ejaculate of dogs living with both smoking and non-smoking owners.

title: Meeting the challenges to adolescent well-being: context, returns on investment, and financing
creator: Peter Sheehan, Bruce Rasmussen, David A Ross, Anshu Mohan, Susan Sawyer, Bhavya Nandini, Levi Singh, Kim Sweeny, John Symons, Rose September
description: Adolescents in many countries face serious challenges in realizing the level of well-being that is their human right. Many factors—deep-seated inequality within and between countries, rapid change in skill requirements for employment, climate change, and social media—are driving these deepening challenges. This paper develops three points about the need for an urgent response to this situation.

title: Hidden causal inference delineates dynamic lncRNA regulation in autism spectrum disorder
creator: Junpeng Zhang, Xuemei Wei, Chunwen Zhao, Zidan Hu, Shujie Fan
description: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are increasingly implicated in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet their dynamic regulatory roles remain poorly characterized. Conventional static causal inference methods are limited in capturing the dynamic interplay of lncRNAs across diverse brain biological contexts. Here, we develop DCRNet (Dynamic Causal Regulation Network), a hidden causality-based framework to infer lncRNA regulatory relationships in ASD.

title: Levels of Stress in Volleyball Referees During Official Matches—The Influence of the Referee Role and Level of Competition
creator: Zoran Nikolovski, Dario Vrdoljak, Nikola Foretić, Mia Perić, Vladimir Pavlinović, Ratko Perić, Vuk Karanović, Kevin Till
description: Volleyball referees, as athletes and staff members, are exposed to different stress levels which can be determined by measuring pre- and post-match levels of salivary cortisol (C) and alpha-amylase (AA). This study aimed to determine the dynamics of stress biomarkers in referees during official volleyball matches and the connection to the roles or level of competition.

title: Characterization of the External Load of Soccer Goalkeepers Depending on the Category and Sports Context
creator: Víctor Hernández-Beltrán, Boryi A. Becerra-Patiño, Abian Perdomo-Alonso, Jesús Barguerias-Martínez, Sergio Gómez-Carrero, Mário C. Espada, José M. Gamonales
description: Background/Objectives: Studies focused on the soccer goalkeeper position in training and official matches are scarce. The present study aimed to analyze the external load during training sessions and official matches in semi-professional goalkeepers. Methods: Data from goalkeepers (n = 6) from the youth ranks of a professional team belonging to the first Spanish soccer league have been used.

title: A Systematic Review of Controlled Trials: Can Patient Adherence to Antibiotics Be Improved Through Pharmaceutical Communication-Based Interventions?
creator: Carla Pires, Majdi N Al-Hasan
